Bimodal age distribution: adolescent growth-spurt peak (10–20y; long-bone metaphyses) and elderly secondary peak (>60y; predominantly Paget disease-associated or post-radiation). Standard-of-care multi-modal treatment (full Indications pending): neoadjuvant chemotherapy → en-bloc surgical resection (limb-salvage preferred; amputation reserved for unresectable / vascular-bundle invasion) → adjuvant chemotherapy. MAP regimen (high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin, cisplatin) is the global standard from EURAMOS-1 (good-responder arm). Histological necrosis ≥90% at resection predicts favorable outcome; poor responders (<90% necrosis) do NOT benefit from intensification per EURAMOS-1. Ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor in any: Ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor in any child / adolescent / young adult should trigger DICER1 germline testing — the proportion of DICER1-positive cases is high (~30-60%, higher in younger and poorly-differentiated cases). Diagnosis in a postmenopausal woman has a lower (though non-zero) DICER1-positive yield. Treatment: fertility-sparing unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (USO) with staging for stage IA well-differentiated tumors in young women; total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TAH-BSO) for postmenopausal patients or high-grade / advanced-stage disease. Adjuvant chemotherapy (BEP — bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin — similar to germ-cell tumour regimens) for stage IC and above, or poorly-differentiated / retiform variants. Androgen excess resolves dramatically post-surgery (virilization symptoms regress but voice deepening may be permanent). Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for germline-positive survivors: contralateral ovary US q6-12 months (synchronous and metachronous DICER1-driven SLCTs reported), chest imaging (PPB risk in survivors' offspring + own residual risk), thyroid US, and abdominal-pelvic US.

PDGFRA D842V substitution mutation in advanced or metastatic GIST. The PDGFRA D842V variant accounts for approximately 6-7% of all GIST and is the most common PDGFRA exon 18 mutation (~65-70% of PDGFRA-mutant GIST). D842V confers primary resistance to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib due to steric interference with drug binding at the activation loop. The type I kinase inhibitor avapritinib binds the active conformation of PDGFRA D842V and achieves ORR ~88% (NAVIGATOR phase 1; Heinrich CANCER DISCOV 2020) and confirmed ORR ~91% in the phase 3 NAVIGATOR expansion cohort. Imatinib is ineffective (historical ORR <10% for D842V) and must not be used as 1L for confirmed D842V-mutant GIST. Fires to route ALGO-GIST-1L step 1 to avapritinib (IND-GIST-1L- AVAPRITINIB-PDGFRA-D842V) instead of imatinib (IND-GIST-1L-IMATINIB). PDGFRA D842V substitution mutation in advanced or metastatic GIST. The PDGFRA D842V variant accounts for approximately 6-7% of all GIST and is the most common PDGFRA exon 18 mutation (~65-70% of PDGFRA-mutant GIST). D842V confers primary resistance to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib due to steric interference with drug binding at the activation loop. The type I kinase inhibitor avapritinib binds the active conformation of PDGFRA D842V and achieves ORR ~88% (NAVIGATOR phase 1; Heinrich CANCER DISCOV 2020) and confirmed ORR ~91% in the phase 3 NAVIGATOR expansion cohort. Imatinib is ineffective (historical ORR <10% for D842V) and must not be used as 1L for confirmed D842V-mutant GIST. Fires to route ALGO-GIST-1L step 1 to avapritinib (IND-GIST-1L- AVAPRITINIB-PDGFRA-D842V) instead of imatinib (IND-GIST-1L-IMATINIB). NCCN GIST 2025 Category 1 preferred: avapritinib 300 mg PO QD for PDGFRA D842V-mutant unresectable/metastatic GIST. Detection: PDGFRA D842V is detectable on targeted NGS, hotspot PCR, or PDGFRA-specific IHC (D842V antibody). Tissue or ctDNA-based molecular testing of all GIST at diagnosis is standard of care per NCCN GIST 2025. PDGFRA non-D842V exon 18 mutations (e.g., D842del, DI842-843IM): intermediate imatinib sensitivity — these are NOT covered by this RF. The RF fires exclusively on the D842V substitution. Non-D842V exon 18 PDGFRA mutations route to imatinib (ALGO-GIST-1L step 2 default path).

Second primary malignancy (SPM) risk: the combination of ASCT + extended lenalidomide increases SPM risk (MDS/AML ~2-3% at 5 yr, solid tumors). Must be included in pre-consent discussion. Phenotype includes attenuated polyposis with early-onset CRC, endometrial cancer, and CNS tumors in some families. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (Lynch-like): colonoscopy q1-2y starting age 20-25, endometrial sampling + TVUS q1-2y from age 30-35 in women (consider earlier given higher endometrial risk than POLE), EGD q3y from age 30, urinalysis q1y from age 30. Risk-reducing hysterectomy + BSO after childbearing is reasonable to discuss in POLD1 carriers (analogous to Lynch INTENSIFIED-track decision). ESCAT IIA.

PTCH1 (Patched-1) is the primary tumor s: PTCH1 (Patched-1) is the primary tumor suppressor in the Hedgehog (HH) pathway. It normally inhibits SMO by sequestering it; when HH ligand (SHH, DHH, IHH) binds PTCH1, this inhibition is released, allowing SMO to activate GLI1/2 transcription factors. Somatic PTCH1 loss is the dominant driver of sporadic BCC (~90%). Germline PTCH1 mutation causes Gorlin syndrome (Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome): multiple BCCs from early adulthood, odontogenic keratocysts, skeletal anomalies, calcified falx cerebri, and markedly increased medulloblastoma risk (SHH-subtype, predominantly desmoplastic, in childhood). Gorlin syndrome patients are exquisitely sensitive to ionizing radiation (radiation-induced BCCs within field); radiation therapy is relatively contraindicated for BCC treatment in Gorlin patients. Therapeutic implication: loss of PTCH1 in BCC justifies hedgehog inhibitor (vismodegib/sonidegib) for locally advanced/metastatic disease — routine tumor PTCH1 testing is not required because HH pathway activation is universal in BCC.

Germline RET testing is mandatory at diagnosis — drives: - Prophylactic thyroidectomy timing in kindred (MEN2B: <1 yr; MEN2A C634: <5 yr per ATA risk classification). - Pheochromocytoma screening (plasma metanephrines / urinary catechols annually) — RET drives both MTC and adrenal medullary tumors. - Hyperparathyroidism screening in MEN2A. Therapy: - Localized: total thyroidectomy + central compartment LN dissection. - Advanced / unresectable (calcitonin doubling time <1 yr or structural progression): selpercatinib (LIBRETTO-001 / -531) or pralsetinib (ARROW) for RET-mutant MTC — superior to multikinase TKIs (vandetanib ZETA / cabozantinib EXAM remain alternatives, significant toxicity). - RET-WT (RAS-mutant or other): no targeted option; cabozantinib / vandetanib by default. Calcitonin doubling time <6 months portends very poor survival; <2 yr drives systemic-therapy decisions even without RECIST progression.

Patient has a confirmed germline pathogenic variant in SMARCB1 (chromosome 22q11.2) or SMARCA4 (chromosome 19p13.2), defining rhabdoid tumor predisposition syndrome type 1 (RTPS1) or type 2 (RTPS2) respectively. Autosomal-dominant inheritance with near-100% penetrance for early-childhood disease in classic SMARCB1 cases. Cancer spectrum: atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor (ATRT) of the CNS with infancy peak, extracranial malignant rhabdoid tumor (MRT) of kidney / liver / soft tissue, small cell carcinoma of the ovary hypercalcemic type (SCCOHT — SMARCA4 specifically), and schwannomatosis in adolescent / adult survivors. The risk window is extremely narrow (peak ATRT incidence in the first 2 years of life) so high-cadence early surveillance is non-negotiable. Prevention-persona confirmed-carrier RedFlag (§20).

Patient-specific autologous polyclonal c: Patient-specific autologous polyclonal cell-therapy product manufactured ex vivo from a fresh resected tumor specimen (typically a single ≥1.5 cm cutaneous, subcutaneous, lymph-node, or visceral metastasis). Pediatric VAC + IE (Ewing-like) protocol: Pediatric VAC + IE (Ewing-like) protocols are myelosuppressive and require strict hepatic / renal monitoring in infants (often <1 yr old). LVEF threshold 55% (not 50%) in pediatric oncology reflects long-life-expectancy sensitivity to anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Larotrectinib / entrectinib much better tolerated than cytotoxic in this age group — the organ-dysfunction flag pushes harder toward TRK-inhibitor monotherapy when fusion-positive (which is >90% of cases). For TRK-inhibitor: dose by BSA / weight per FDA pediatric label; hepatic dose reduction required at bilirubin >3× ULN.
Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DI: Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents + siblings. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is a separate (non- DICER1) etiology that shares the Wilms-spectrum abdominal-tumour surveillance protocol (abdominal US q3-4 months from birth to age 7; AFP q2-3 months from birth to age 4 — focused on hepatoblastoma). Treatment: maximal safe surgical resection (nephron-sparing partial nephrectomy when anatomically feasible; total nephrectomy if not). Histopathology after resection is critical — distinguishes pure cystic nephroma (benign-borderline, surveillance only) from cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma (Wilms-spectrum, requires adjuvant chemo per stage) and from progression to anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney (high-grade malignant, requires multimodal therapy). Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for germline-positive survivors: chest imaging (PPB risk), abdominal-pelvic US (ovarian, Sertoli-Leydig risk in girls), thyroid US, and CNS imaging (pineoblastoma, pituitary blastoma risk under age 5).
Pediatric infection screening is broader: Pediatric infection screening is broader than adult — include CMV / herpes given immunosuppression on VAC and likelihood of reactivation in neonates / infants. HBsAg+ infants: confirm vertical transmission, consult pediatric hepatology, entecavir / tenofovir prophylaxis adapted to weight. HIV+ pediatric: ART coordination critical — TRK inhibitors (larotrectinib, entrectinib) are CYP3A4 substrates, avoid CYP3A4 inhibitors. Pneumocystis prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) is standard on cytotoxic arm. Surfaces hold via parallel pre-treatment workup.

Pexidartinib (PLX3397), a CSF1R/KIT/FLT3 inhibitor, is FDA-approved (August 2019) for adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) associated with severe morbidity or functional limitations not amenable to improvement with surgery. ILLUMINATE phase III trial (Tap et al., Lancet 2019): N=120 (pexidartinib vs placebo, crossover design); primary endpoint ORR at week 25 by RECIST 1.1 and TTP-MRI. ORR: 38% (RECIST) vs 0% placebo (p<0.0001); 56% by TTP-MRI vs 0%. mDOR: not reached at median 23.1 months follow-up. Clinical benefit rate: 56%. Safety: significant hepatotoxicity (cholestatic hepatitis, including one fatal case in open-label extension); ALT/AST elevations in ~51%; FDA REMS program mandatory. EMA approved for same indication (2020). No biomarker companion diagnostic required — all TGCT patients are eligible based on clinical criteria (symptomatic, surgery-resistant). CSF1R IHC or COL6A3-CSF1 fusion testing is not required for treatment initiation.

Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secr: Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor of adrenal medullary origin; extra-adrenal counterparts (paragangliomas) arise from sympathetic / parasympathetic ganglia (head/neck, thoracic, abdominal). They are biologically and clinically a single spectrum (PPGL); this entity is anchored to the adrenal subset for ICD-10 cleanliness but cross-references SDHx-driven extra-adrenal paragangliomas in prevention workstream notes. Hereditary fraction is the highest known among adult cancers (~30–40%). NCCN and Endocrine Society recommend germline panel testing (RET, VHL, SDHB/C/D/AF2, NF1, TMEM127, MAX, FH) for ALL patients with PPGL — not restricted by family history. This makes PPGL a sentinel disease for hereditary cancer surveillance pathways (RET → MEN2 prophylactic thyroidectomy; VHL → multi-organ surveillance; SDHB → lifetime PPGL + RCC surveillance). Classical clinical triad: headache + palpitations + sweating; many patients present with paroxysmal or sustained hypertension. Active moiety blocks the substance P / NK1 receptor in CNS emetic centers (nucleus tractus solitarius, area postrema), preventing the delayed phase of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) that is incompletely controlled by 5-HT3 antagonists alone. A single 150 mg IV dose given on day 1 covers the full delayed phase (~5 days), eliminating need for oral days 2-3 capsules. Approved by FDA January 2008 (single-dose 150 mg formulation: October 2008) and EMA January 2008.

Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical em: Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical embryonal CNS manifestations of DICER1 syndrome — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing regardless of family history. Distinct from pineocytoma (Grade 1, benign) and pineal parenchymal tumour of intermediate differentiation (PPTID, Grade 2-3). Treatment philosophy parallels other embryonal CNS tumours: maximal safe surgical resection (gross total resection is prognostically dominant); craniospinal irradiation in age-appropriate patients (deferred under age 3 due to neurocognitive toll); adjuvant high-dose chemotherapy regimens (often COG/SIOP protocols with carboplatin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, cisplatin, etoposide combinations + autologous stem-cell rescue in high-risk cases). Trilateral retinoblastoma (bilateral RB1-carrier with pineal pineoblastoma) historically had near-uniform mortality; modern MRI surveillance from RB1-carrier diagnosis has shifted some cases to earlier detection with improved outcomes.

Piperacillin is a ureidopenicillin that: Piperacillin is a ureidopenicillin that binds penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis, producing rapid bactericidal activity against most Gram-negative bacilli including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, most Enterobacterales, many anaerobes, and selected Gram-positive cocci. Tazobactam is an irreversible β-lactamase inhibitor (penicillanic acid sulfone) that binds and inactivates plasmid-mediated and chromosomal class A β-lactamases (TEM, SHV, CTX-M ESBLs partially), restoring piperacillin activity against many β-lactamase-producing organisms. First-line empiric monotherapy for febrile neutropenia (FN) at most centers per IDSA, ECIL-4, and NCCN guidelines because of pseudomonal coverage, anaerobic activity, and good safety profile.

Pituitary blastoma is the strongest sing: Pituitary blastoma is the strongest single-tumour DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any infant should immediately trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents (>95% pituitary blastomas carry pathogenic germline DICER1). Distinct from far-more- common pituitary adenomas (which are not DICER1-driven and are typically adult-onset). Treatment: trans-sphenoidal or trans-cranial resection (technically challenging in infants — pituitary blastomas are bleeding-prone and locally invasive); adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-VP16-cyclophosphamide-based regimens reported in case series); RT generally avoided under age 3 due to severe neurocognitive + endocrine toll. Hypercortisolism management (medical adrenal blockade, sometimes adrenalectomy) is an essential pre-operative bridge. Lifelong endocrine replacement (hydrocortisone, growth hormone, thyroid, gonadal axis) after curative-intent resection. Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for survivors.

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) with persistent anovulation and resulting chronic unopposed estrogen exposure on endometrial epithelium — endometrial cancer RR ~2.7 (Haoula et al. Hum Reprod Update 2012); earlier age of onset (40s vs typical 60s) common. Often accompanied by obesity + insulin resistance + type-2 diabetes — additional independent endometrial-cancer risk factors that compound risk multiplicatively. Endometrioid (type I) histology predominates. Frequently underrecognized in women relying on hormonal contraception that masks anovulation. Risk modifiable: combined hormonal contraception (estrogen + progestin) OR cyclic progestin OR levonorgestrel IUD restore endometrial protection. Weight loss + metformin (in T2DM/IR PCOS) provide additional risk reduction. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 reproductive expansion).

Pre-existing autoimmune disease is prese: Pre-existing autoimmune disease is present in ~10-15% of patients eligible for ICI therapy; historically excluded from pivotal trials. Risk stratification by SITC 2021: - **Low risk** (generally safe to proceed with monitoring): thyroiditis, vitiligo, stable psoriasis, type 1 diabetes — irAE flare mild, manageable. - **Moderate risk** (proceed with specialist input): RA, IBD (Crohn/UC), sarcoidosis, sicca syndrome, psoriatic arthritis — flare rate ~50%; baseline DMARDs often OK to continue (methotrexate, HCQ but NOT high-dose steroids or anti-TNF at start). - **High risk** (strongest caution; consider alternative if available): active autoimmune hepatitis, myasthenia gravis, inflammatory myopathy, neuromyelitis optica — flare can be life-threatening; benefit-risk discussion mandatory. Pulmonary sarcoidosis specifically: ICI-induced sarcoid-like reactions are well-documented (5-7% of patients on ICI), often mimicking disease progression on imaging. Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and f: Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and for multi-day chemotherapy regimens because of long half-life and demonstrated superiority in delayed-phase CINV control vs ondansetron in head-to-head trials (Saito 2009, Aapro 2014). Triple antiemetic regimen for HEC: NK1 antagonist (aprepitant or fosaprepitant) + palonosetron 0.25 mg IV + dexamethasone 12 mg IV day 1, with dex tapered through delayed phase. Akynzeo (netupitant 300 mg + palonosetron 0.5 mg) fixed-dose oral capsule simplifies triple therapy to two pills (Akynzeo + dex) on day 1. Lowest QT signal in 5-HT3 class — preferred when ondansetron contraindicated due to QT concerns or cardiac comorbidity. Minimal CYP-mediated metabolism makes it the safer 5-HT3 choice in polypharmacy patients (e.g., patients on CYP3A4 inhibitors).
Preferred BTKi for CLL 1L per NCCN 2025: Preferred BTKi for CLL 1L per NCCN 2025 (over ibrutinib due to less cardiac toxicity). ELEVATE-TN (1L CLL): superior PFS vs Clb+O at 5y; ELEVATE-RR (r/r): non-inferior to ibrutinib with better safety. Funding pathway must be confirmed pre-start in Ukraine.
Preferred BTKi over ibrutinib in modern: Foretrukket BTKi framfor ibrutinib i moderne retningslinjer for CLL/MCL (ELEVATE-RR for r/r CLl — sammenlignbar effektivitet, færre hjerte/hypertension-hendelser). Fires when patient profile shows chronic H. pylori (positive UBT / stool antigen / biopsy histology / stool PCR) AND no confirmed gastric malignancy. Evidence for H. pylori → gastric cancer causation (IARC Group 1): multiple Cochrane meta-analyses show eradication reduces gastric adenocarcinoma incidence (RR ~0.54-0.66, NNT ~15-50 depending on population baseline incidence). Effect is stronger in high-incidence populations and in younger individuals where atrophic gastritis / intestinal metaplasia has not yet developed. Evidence for H. pylori → gastric MALT lymphoma: eradication is the first-line treatment for early-stage gastric MALT lymphoma, with Wotherspoon regression in ~70-80% of cases (especially t(11;18)- negative). This is treatment-persona territory (existing MALT lymphoma in setting of confirmed H. pylori → treatment Indication, not yet authored) — distinct from prevention persona (chronic H. pylori → prevent MALT/adenocarc...

Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic HCV (HCV-RNA detectable OR HCV-Ab+ with persistent viremia >6 months) AND no confirmed B-cell NHL diagnosis. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending DAA antiviral therapy (per IND-CHRONIC-HCV-PREVENTION-DAA) as the etiological-cancer-prevention pathway. Evidence for HCV → NHL causation (IARC Group 1): multiple cohort studies show 2-3x increased risk of indolent B-cell NHL in chronic HCV carriers; epidemiology especially robust for MZL subtypes. DAA cure (SVR12) has been associated with reduced NHL incidence in post-treatment cohorts (de-Re et al. and others) and with regression of established HCV-associated indolent NHL (the basis of IND-HCV-MZL-1L-ANTIVIRAL for the treatment persona). This is a STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode exemption (sources cited, draft flag set). Coexists with existing RF-LIFESTYLE-PROCESSED-MEAT-PREVENTION — both may fire.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for ATM heter: Prevention-persona RedFlag for ATM heterozygous carriers. Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance + pancreatic surveillance for FDR-of- PDAC carriers per CAPS consortium 2022; prostate awareness for males. Prevention-persona RedFlag for BRIP1 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BRIP1 heterozygous carriers. Prevention-persona RedFlag for C. sinens: Prevention-persona RedFlag for C. sinensis-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. East-Asian endemic belt has 10-50x higher cholangiocarcinoma incidence than non-endemic Western populations. Geographic context: relevant for East-Asian diaspora, immigrants, refugees, adoptees. Companion to RF-OPISTHORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (Mekong-region liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism — identical surveillance protocol).

Prophylaktisk total gastrectomy (PTG) anbefalt alder 20-30 (intervall 18-40 per individualisert diskusjon); endoskopisk overvåking anerkjennes som mindre enn PTG (tvær av signet-ringingcelle foci av typen diffuse) som er dårlig synlig) men tilbys PTS-tykkende luftfartsselskap. Hunntransportører: BRCA-lignende brystovervåking fra 30 år. STUB i påvente av to-co-lead-avtegning per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDKN2A-sp: Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDKN2A-specific carriers (gene-specific RF vs the broader FAMMM RF). Pancreatic surveillance per CAPS Consortium 2018/2020: alternating EUS + abdominal MRI/MRCP every 12 months from age 40 OR 10 years before earliest PDAC in family (whichever earlier). Patient should know aggressive sun protection + lifelong CDKN2A-specific cohort. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CHEK2 het: Forebyggende person RedFlag for heterozygote CHEK2- bærere. Risikoestimatene varierer betydelig etter variant: slitelag > splice > oversvømmelse. Motorveier til forsterket brystovervåking (årlig mammografi fra 40 års alder + MRI- vurdering), beskjedent skjerpet CRC- gjennomsøking (kolonoskopi fra 40 år med q5y-intervall per NCCN) og prostatabevissthet fra 40-45 års alder for menn med c.1100delC. STUB i påvente av to- Co-Lead- tegn per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CMMRD con: Forebyggende person RedFlag for CMMRD bekreftet barne- og foreldrekohort. STUB i påvente av to-Co-Lead avtegn per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Mortality reduced markedly with immuno- suppression treatment. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DES in-ut: Forebyggende person-slagg for DES in-utero eksponeringskohort. Overvåkingen skjerpes i forhold til den generelle befolkningen (årlig bækkenkar med nøye vaginal/servikal inspeksjon, kolposkopi dersom unormal cytologi, mammografi ved yngre aldersterskel per NCCN-modifikatorrisiko, overvei MRI-screening med doblet risiko). STUB fram til to-co-lead-avtegning per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DICER1 co: Forebyggende og person- RedFlag for DICER1 bekreftet smitteforhold. Pediatrisk overvåking pr. internasjonal PPB- registrering / IDSDB anbefalinger: – Brøst CT q4-6 mo fra fødsel til alder 3, q6-12 mo til alder 8. – Abdominal US q3-6 mo etter fødsel til aldersgruppen 8. – Skjaldbruskkjertel US baseline etter alder 8 + q3-5 y. – Pelvic US hos kvinnelige bærere fra menarke. – Hjerne MRI baseline + symptomdrevet. STUB venter på to- Co- Lead avtegning per CHARTER §6.1 dev- mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-drive: Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-driven cancer prevention in immunocompromised hosts. Unlike HCV/HBV/H. pylori, there is no curative anti-EBV regimen; the prevention pathway is (a) reduce immunosuppression where feasible, (b) preemptive rituximab in post-transplant patients with rising EBV-DNA (per international PTLD guidelines), (c) periodic EBV-DNA monitoring. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Gating by additional immunocompromise context is deliberate — EBV seroprevalence is >90% in immunocompetent adults globally, so a RF triggered on EBV alone would fire universally and provide no clinical signal.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for FAMMM / C: Forebyggende person RedFlag for FAMMM / CDKN2A. STUB på avtegning med to Co-Lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on HBsAg+ OR detectable HBV-DNA in patient without HCC. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending nucleos(t)ide analog suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HBV-PREVENTION-ANTIVIRAL) + AFP+US HCC surveillance q6mo per AASLD protocol. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchor target DIS-HCC. HBV-associated DLBCL/NHL is also documented in literature but with weaker effect-size data than the HCV-NHL link; covered via the broader NHL prevention surveillance bullet in the antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-UNIVERSAL-HBV-REACTIVATION-RISK (existing) which is the treatment-time RF for HBV reactivation during anti-CD20 / chemo.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than either mono-infection RF — coinfection carries documented synergistic HCC risk AND DAA-cure-induced HBV reactivation risk that requires combination antiviral. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending concurrent DAA + nucleos(t)ide analog + intensified HCC surveillance (US + AFP q4-6mo, more frequent than the q6mo cadence for either mono-infection). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. NHL prevention (HCV-driven) continues to be a secondary benefit; tracked via prose in the combined-antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HCV-NHL-PREVENTION-OPPORTUNITY and RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence over the two individual RFs (higher priority).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-dri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-driven malignancy prevention. Fires on HHV-8 seropositivity in HIV+, transplant, or other immunocompromised host without confirmed Kaposi sarcoma / MCD / PEL. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending immune restoration (ART for HIV+; transplant-immunosuppression rebalance) + mucocutaneous + oral + GI / lymph-node surveillance. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-KAPOSI. MCD and PEL are HHV-8-driven but not yet authored as distinct Disease entities — covered via the prose surveillance rationale in the indication for now. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (existing) — that is HIV-as-RF; this is HHV-8-positivity-as-RF (the co-factor that turns HIV-related immunocompromise into Kaposi risk specifically).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than mono-infection HBV RF — coinfection carries documented accelerated-fibrosis + elevated HCC risk AND a hard constraint on antiviral selection (tenofovir-based ART mandatory; entecavir monotherapy contraindicated). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending tenofovir-based ART (covers both viruses simultaneously) + AASLD HCC surveillance q6mo. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. HIV-driven AIDS-defining malignancies (Kaposi sarcoma via HHV-8 reactivation, NHL, cervical) are covered separately via RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HHV8-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence (higher priority) and the indication enforces tenofovir-based ART selection.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on positive HIV serology in patient without AIDS-defining or HIV-associated malignancy. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending durable ART suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HIV-PREVENTION-ART) + cancer screening cadence (annual anal cytology in MSM/HIV+; q3-yearly cervical Pap in WLHIV; opportunistic Kaposi/oral hairy leukoplakia visual screening). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the canonical HIV-associated NHL. KS, cervical, anal, Hodgkin, HCC are also HIV-associated; covered via screening recommendations in the ART indication rationale rather than discrete Disease anchors (until DIS-KAPOSI etc. land in v0.2-A authoring backlog).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPRC. STU: Forebyggende person RedFlag for HPRC. STUB på avtegning med to med leader.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on persistent high-risk HPV positivity OR incomplete/absent vaccination in age-eligible individual. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending vaccination (Gardasil-9) and/or risk-group-appropriate screening cadence (cervical: USPSTF Pap+HPV co-test q5y ages 30-65; anal: HRA + cytology q1y in MSM/HIV+/post-transplant). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CERVICAL and DIS-ANAL-SCC. Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma and vulvar/vaginal/penile not yet in KB — v0.2-A authoring backlog.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-dr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-driven ATLL prevention. Unlike HCV/HBV/H. pylori, there is no curative regimen — the intervention is surveillance + transmission prevention, not cure. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Geographic context: HTLV-1 endemic regions include Japan (southwest), Caribbean basin, parts of sub-Saharan Africa, parts of South America, Middle East. Ukraine is low-prevalence; this RF is more relevant for diaspora patients or those with travel/origin from endemic regions.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 the: Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 therapeutic-dose lifetime cumulative exposure. Surveillance: CBC q12mo for leukemia signal (sensitivity modest); breast surveillance per general-population USPSTF unless additional risk factors; oral + salivary symptom awareness. Highest-impact preventive intervention is hydration + lemon-juice sialagogue during I-131 administration (reduces salivary gland uptake) — retrospectively non-actionable for prior exposure. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAF: Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAFLD HCC risk. Cirrhotic MASLD meets AASLD HCC-surveillance threshold (US ± AFP q6mo). Non-cirrhotic advanced fibrosis is a gray zone — closer hepatology follow-up but not yet routine surveillance. Major actionable lever: weight loss + cardiometabolic management. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confi: Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confirmed-carrier / clinical- diagnostic-criteria-met cohort. Multi-organ surveillance: pediatric ophthalmology q6-12mo to age 8 (optic glioma); whole-body MRI for MPNST surveillance + symptom-driven biopsy of growing/painful/ neurologically-symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas; women: annual mammography from age 30, MRI from age 30-50. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverrini-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. Northeast Thailand has the world's highest cholangiocarcinoma incidence (up to 90 per 100K) — attributable fraction in endemic regions exceeds 50%. Geographic context: relevant for Mekong-region diaspora, refugees, travelers, and adoptees. Companion to RF-CLONORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (East Asian liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 het: Forebyggende person RedFlag for heterozygote PALB2-bærere. PAL B2-metoden nærmer seg BRCA2-gjennomtrenging av brystkreft og garanterer årlig overvåking av BRCA-aktige bryst MRI + mammografi fra 30 års alder, samt overvåking av pankreas (EUS eller MRI vekselvis fra 50 års alder eller 10 år før den tidligste PTC-typen i familie) for FDR-of-PDAC-bærere per CAPS-konsortium 2022. RRSO-forhandlingen utsatt til terskelen for BRCA i BRCA som er gitt lavere penetrans. STUB i påvente av to-co-lead avtegning per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anov: Forebyggende person RedFlag for PCOS-anovuleringsrisikoen for endometriale risikoer. Skillet fra den brede reproduktive RF for klarere ruting — PCOS - spesifikk rådgivning (progestin restaurering, metformin, vekttap) skiller seg fra generisk reproduktiv rådgivning. Symptom-drevet endometriebiopsi ved unormal blødning ≥ 6 måneders amenorhea premenopaus eller eventuell postmenopeusal blødning. STUB i påvente av to-co-bly-signal per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RA: Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RAD51D heterozygous carriers. Approaches BRCA-level ovarian penetrance — NCCN endorses RRSO at completed childbearing or age 45-50. Breast surveillance: individualised by family history; consider annual MRI in additional- risk subset. Olaparib PARP inhibitor active in RAD51C/D-mutant established ovarian cancer (PROfound + GEN-ALL trials). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haemat: Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haematobium-driven bladder SCC prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifetime urinary surveillance (urinalysis q6-12mo, cytology + cystoscopy for any new hematuria). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL. S. haematobium-driven bladder cancers are predominantly SCC histology (distinct from urothelial / transitional cell carcinoma that dominates Western cohorts) — engine surfaces this distinction in the prevention rationale prose. Geographic context: Ukraine is non-endemic; this RF is relevant for patients with diaspora / refugee / travel / origin history from sub-Saharan Africa, Egypt, Sudan, Yemen, parts of South America.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for SDH-defic: Prevention-persona RedFlag for SDH-deficiency syndrome. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for active to: Forebyggende person RedFlag for bruk av aktiv tobakk. Modifiserbar kreftrisikofaktor med høyest virkning. Motorveier til forebyggingPlan anbefaler strukturert stopprådgivning + farmakoterapi + LDCT lungescreening hvis USPSTF- støtte. STUB venter på to- klinisk- co- leid avtegning pr CHARTER §6.1 dev- mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracyc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracycline cumulative dose ≥250 mg/m². Cardio surveillance focus (HF / cardiomyopathy); t-AML surveillance overlap covered by separate RF-IATROGENIC-TOPO2-TAML-PREVENTION. Echo q1-5y depending on risk profile (ASCO/COG-LTFU cadence). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending baseline + serial echo + BNP. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-: Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-amines → urothelial bladder cancer prevention. Fires on documented occupational exposure. DIS-UROTHELIAL anchor preferred but using DIS-HCC as fallback if not in KB on this branch. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic E: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ETS exposure (household / workplace ≥10y). IARC Group 1 + US Surgeon General-confirmed cause of lung cancer in non-smokers. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum. Distinct from active-smoking RF. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure elimination (cohabitant smoking cessation / workplace smoke-free policy enforcement / personal mitigation) + USPSTF screening eligibility check + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic P: Forebyggende person RedFlag for kronisk eksponering for PPI ≥10y. Motorveier til forebyggingsplan som anbefaler (1) indikasjonsvurdering + avreskresjon der det ikke lenger er behov for PPP (mest vanlig scenario), 2) fastgastrin + kromogran A i kohort med vedvarende syresuppressiv indikasjon, 3) EGD med kropps-/fundusbiopsier hos personer med hevet gastrin eller symptomer, overvåking EGD q3-5y dersom atriske gastritis eller ECL hyperplasi er dokumentert. Forankret til DIS-GASTRIC (mage-NET og atrologisk-gastritis-derivert adenokarcinom begge mage- og kroppssykdommer); NET-spesifikke resultater medført i indikasjonsprose. STUB i påvente av to-klinisk-co-lead-skilt per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic a: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic anti-TNF biologic exposure ≥3y in pediatric / adolescent / young-adult IBD cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) EBV serology baseline in young adults, (2) B-symptom + lymphadenopathy awareness, (3) annual skin examination (synergistic with concomitant thiopurine + UV), (4) periodic shared-decision discussion of combination- therapy step-down where IBD activity allows (anti-TNF monotherapy has favourable cancer signal vs combination with thiopurine), (5) vaccination catch-up (HPV, HBV, influenza, pneumococcal). Severity = minor — absolute attributable risk in anti-TNF monotherapy is small; the meaningful signal is the combination- with-thiopurine HSTCL warning specifically in pediatric / young- adult cohort, addressed via combination-step-down counseling. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS + DIS-HSTCL. STUB pending two-Clinical- Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic i: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic inorganic arsenic exposure via drinking water >10 µg/L (WHO + US EPA MCL). IARC Group 1 carcinogen with established urothelial, lung, and non-melanoma skin cancer etiology. Anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL per task brief; lung + skin surfaced via relevant_diseases. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending water source change / filtration + intensified screening for affected organs. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic o: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic occupational outdoor UV exposure ≥10y in high-UV-index latitudes. IARC Group 1 solar UV. Distinct from broader RF-LIFESTYLE-UV-EXPOSURE-PREVENTION (which covers tanning beds + sunburn history + recreational UV). Anchored to DIS-BCC per task brief (closest skin DIS to UV-NMSC). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending photoprotection counseling + clinical skin exam cadence + patient skin self-exam education + Vitamin D balance. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic p: Forebyggende og personskadelig rødflagg for kronisk pankreatit → PDAC. Hereditær pankreas innebærer høy risiko (~40-50% levetid).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic r: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic residential PM2.5 >35 µg/m³ annual average (WHO 2021 IT-1). IARC Group 1 outdoor air pollution + PM. Population-attributable fraction modest individually but large absolute burden in high-exposure regions including industrial Ukraine + during war-related fire / debris events. risk_category=occupational is the closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum (§20 ratification pending). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure reduction + USPSTF lung-cancer screening eligibility + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥3y post-transplant immunosuppression cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan with long-cycle surveillance cadence appropriate to the chronic cohort (vs the acute-window EBV-DNA cadence in the new-transplant RF). Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TRANSPLANT-IMMUNOSUPPRESSION- PREVENTION (which covers acute / new-transplant window). Both RFs may fire simultaneously in the early-chronic window (1-3y post-transplant) — engine routes to both surveillance tracks, render layer deduplicates overlapping recommendations. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the primary lymphoma anchor (late- onset PTLD histology more DLBCL-like; DIS-PTLD as the canonical early-onset EBV-driven entity). Multiple cancer types listed in relevant_diseases reflect the broad cumulative-risk profile of the chronic cohort. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined: Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined HRT exposure ≥5y. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) shared-decision discussion of risk-benefit (vasomotor symptoms, bone-density preservation vs breast / VTE / cardiovascular risks), (2) lowest-effective-dose + shortest-duration principle per NAMS / ACOG, (3) breast surveillance per USPSTF cadence — supplemental imaging not recommended on HRT alone (density-related supplemental imaging is a separate axis), (4) symptom-prompted endometrial workup (any abnormal bleeding → TVUS + biopsy) for women on sequential/cyclic combined or with intact uterus on any HRT, (5) annual GYN exam. Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TAMOXIFEN-ENDOMETRIAL-PREVENTION (different mechanism: SERM with partial endometrial agonism). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Forebyggingsperson RedFlag for kombinert lavt kalsiuminntak + vitamin D-mangel. WCRF/AICR-sannsynlighet for kalsium og CRC, IARC-sammenlagt signal for vitamin D. RCT-bevis for tilsetning blandes ved befolkningsdoser — rådgivning legger vekt på at inntak/oppløsning ikke er farmakologisk. Motorveier til forebyggingPlan anbefaler rådgivning gjennom kosten + vitamin B-oppløsning + CRC-screening per USPSTF. STUB i påvente av to-klinisk-co-lead-avtegning per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for cumulativ: Prevention-persona RedFlag for cumulative hormonal-contraception exposure ≥10y, iatrogenic-axis only (exposure-as-risk). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending HPV co-test on schedule per ASCCP / USPSTF, age-appropriate mammographic screening per USPSTF, attentive symptom history (breast lump, abnormal bleeding). Severity minor — absolute risk increment small, effect on breast cancer attenuates after stop. Distinct from RF-REPRODUCTIVE-OCP-LONG-TERM (balanced risk-benefit counseling, see §20 reproductive bucket). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for endometri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for endometriosis-associated ovarian cancer risk. NO routine population-screening tool exists (CA-125 + TVUS not recommended for general or endometriosis screening per NCCN/USPSTF). Counseling: symptom awareness; consider risk-reducing salpingectomy at completed childbearing or at hysterectomy for benign indications; BSO reserved for those with additional risk factors. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for heavy alc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for heavy alcohol use. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending structured cessation/moderation counseling + pharmacotherapy + appropriate cancer screening (esophageal endoscopy for high-risk, breast cancer surveillance for women). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for high cumu: Forebyggende person RedFlag for høy kumulativ UV- eksponering. IARC gruppe 1- klassifisering for solsenger (2009). NCCN Melanoma + AAD retningslinjer støtter UV - rådgivning + hud selveksamen + klinisk hudprøve- kadens. Motorveier til forebyggingPlan anbefaler solbeskyttelse + hudovervåking. STUB i påvente av to- klinisk- ko- lead- avtegning per CHARTER §6.1 dev- mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for high-pari: Forebyggende person RedFlag for høyparitets legsleirrisikoforsterker hos HPV-positive kvinner.Ret: overholdelse av legsliftsscreening etter alder og metode for USPSTF/WHO; oppfanging av HPV vaksinasjon til 45 år pr. ACIP-deltakelse; røykeavbrudd (synergistisk risiko). STUB i påvente av to-co-lead-signering pr. CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for in-utero: Prevention-persona RedFlag for in-utero DES exposure. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending annual gynecologic exam with speculum + bimanual + careful palpation of vaginal walls (specific technique for DES daughters per ACOG), colposcopy with vaginal + cervical staining for early detection of CCA, cervical cytology / HPV co-test on routine cadence, breast surveillance per age- appropriate USPSTF cadence. Cohort is aging — bimodal-risk window extends past 40y; surveillance does NOT stop at any age cutoff. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-VULVAR-VAGINAL-SCC (closest existing Disease entity for vaginal-tract anchor) + DIS-CERVICAL. DES- associated cancer is histologically clear-cell adenocarcinoma — NOT yet authored as a distinct DIS-VAGINAL-CLEAR-CELL entity; histology-specific surveillance considerations carried via the indication prose. Future authoring of DIS-VAGINAL-CLEAR-CELL recommended. Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-LONG-TERM-HRMNL-CONTRACEPTION- PREVENTION (post-natal hormonal exposure, exposure-as-cofactor). This is a one-time in-utero developmental exposure — surveillance cohort is closed (no new DES daughters); known existing cohort remains at lifelong elevated risk.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for late-firs: Prevention-persona RedFlag for late-first-pregnancy + short-breastfeeding combination. Modest individual effect sizes; cumulative effect non-trivial. Cannot retroactively modify primary trigger (timing of reproductive events) — counseling is forward-looking (encourage breastfeeding when feasible in subsequent pregnancies) + tightened breast cancer screening. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term: Forebyggingsperson RedFlag for langvarig kombinert bruk av OCP ≥10y. Blandet kreftprofil — beskjeden risikoøkning (breast, cervikal med HPV) OG betydelig beskyttelse (ovarisk, endometrieal). Motorveier til forebyggingsplan som anbefaler COUNSEL-BALANSEindikasjon, ikke enveis risikoadvarsel. Kritisk at laget utgjør et fullt risiko-nyttepanel. STUB i påvente av to-klinisk-co-lead-signering per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Forebyggende person RedFlag for langsiktig eksponering for lavdose MTX (RA, psoriasis, IBD). Overvåking: lavterskel for opparbeiding av uforklarlig lymfadenopati, B-symptomer, organomegali, masse – MTX-avvenning + observere 8-12 uker først (~50% regress), vedvarende → DLBCL- up. Hudundersøkelse årlig. STUB i påvente av to-co-lead avslag per CHARTER §6.1 dev-modus.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term ≥3y thiopurine (azathioprine / 6-MP) exposure. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) annual whole-body skin exam by dermatologist + aggressive sun-protection counseling, (2) EBV serology baseline check in young adults pre-initiation (avoid initiation in EBV-seronegative young men per ECCO 2019), (3) annual B-symptom + lymphadenopathy review, (4) shared-decision discussion of indication continuation vs alternatives (MTX for RA, biologics for IBD) at year 5, (5) HPV vaccination catch-up where applicable. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS (lymphoma) + DIS-BCC (closest skin-cancer anchor for SCC and BCC). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term ≥5y calcineurin-inhibitor exposure (cyclosporine or tacrolimus). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) annual or q6mo whole-body skin exam by dermatologist (q6mo if any prior skin cancer), (2) aggressive sun-protection counseling, (3) HHV-8 awareness in endemic cohorts + KS surveillance (skin, oral, GI), (4) HPV vaccination catch-up if transplant context, (5) shared-decision discussion with transplant team of switch to mTOR inhibitor (sirolimus / everolimus) in patients with cumulative skin- cancer burden — CONVERT + ProSparc evidence: mTOR-switch reduces new SCC. Anchored to DIS-KAPOSI + DIS-BCC. Distinct from broader RF-IATROGENIC-TRANSPLANT-IMMUNOSUPPRESSION-* RFs by drug-class specificity — applies also to non-transplant calcineurin-inhibitor users (psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, nephrotic syndrome). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for low Medit: Prevention-persona RedFlag for low Mediterranean-diet adherence. Population-level dietary-pattern lever — distinct from single-nutrient RFs (fibre, calcium, red meat). PREDIMED RCT (2013 primary endpoint cardiovascular; 2015 secondary CRC analysis) + EPIC + NHS observational signal. Anchored to DIS-CRC because pattern-cancer evidence is strongest there; multi-cancer benefit framed in rationale. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary-pattern counseling + USPSTF-cadence screening per anchor. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for low dieta: Prevention-persona RedFlag for low dietary fibre intake (<15 g/day). WCRF/AICR convincing-evidence rating for CRC. Effect size modest individually but population-attributable fraction non-trivial (low fibre intake is endemic in Western diets). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary counseling + USPSTF-cadence CRC screening. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for obesity (: Forebyggende person RedFlag for overvekt (BMI ≥ 30) Motorveier til forebyggingsplan som anbefaler strukturert vekttapsintervensjon + bariatrisk kirurgi drøfting i klasse 2/3 overvekt + kreftscreening per BMI-opphevet risikoprofil.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior alk: Forebyggende- person RedFlag for tidligere eksponering for alkylator kemoterapi. Median t- AML latency 5-7y etter eksponering; kumulativ forekomst ~1-10% ved 10y. Motorveier til ForebyggingPlan anbefaler CBC q3- 6mo for første 10y post- chemo + lav terskel for karv evaluering hvis det forekommer cytopenier. STUB i påvente av to- klinisk- Co- Lead avtegn per CHARTER §6.1 dev- mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior the: Forebyggende person RedFlag for tidligere terapeutisk stråling. Barnekreft-studie + LATE-konsortium-dokument økte andre primær malignitetsrisiko tiår etterRT.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior top: Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior topoisomerase-II inhibitor exposure. Distinct from alkylator t-AML: shorter latency (2-3y vs 5-7y), characteristic 11q23/21q22 cytogenetics, often APL-like t(15;17). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending CBC q3mo for first 5y post-chemo + low threshold for marrow evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. Note: anthracycline exposure also fires RF-IATROGENIC-ANTHRACYCLINE-CARDIO-PREVENTION (separate cardio + t-AML surveillance overlap).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for processed: Prevention-persona RedFlag for processed-meat consumption ≥50g/day. WCRF/AICR convincing evidence + IARC Group 1 classification for CRC. Effect size modest individually but population-attributable fraction non-trivial. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary counseling + CRC screening per USPSTF. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for refractor: Forebyggende, person- rødFlag for refraktær celiaki → EATL forebygging. Branner på vedvarende vilde atrofi / aberrant IEL klonalitet / RCD2- objekter. STUB venter på to- klinisk- ko- lead avtegning pr CHARTER §6.1 dev- mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for reproduct: Forebyggende person RedFlag for reproduksjonshistorier. Effektstørrelsene er beskjedne enkeltvis, men kumulative signifikante. STUB i påvente av to-co-lead avtegning.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for salt/pick: Prevention-persona RedFlag for salt/pickle-heavy diet. Counseling: reduce to WHO <5 g/day; co-test for H. pylori in high-intake + high-prevalence settings (Eastern Europe, East Asia); diet-quality intervention (Mediterranean / DASH patterns) provides additional cardiovascular benefit. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for sedentary: Forebyggende og personlig RødFlag for sedentær livsstil / lav fysisk aktivitet. WCRF/ AICR overbevisende bevis for CRC + endometrial + beskyttelse av brystkreft etter menopausalitet. Motorruter til forebyggingPlaner for strukturert fysisk aktivitetsrådgivning etter HHS + ACS retningslinjer. STUB i påvente av toklinisk- Co- Lead avtegning pr CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for smokeless: Prevention-persona RedFlag for smokeless tobacco. Most modifiable cancer exposure in users; cessation pharmacotherapy (nicotine replacement, varenicline) is effective. Oral examination at every encounter; biopsy any leukoplakia/erythroplakia >2 weeks; visual inspection with toluidine blue or autofluorescence in high-burden settings. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for sugar-swe: Forebyggende og personlig rødflag for vanlig inntak av sukkersøtte drikker. Rådgivning: erstatning for vann/usøtede drikker, redusere gradvis dersom det er vanskelig å plutselig stanse; vurdere for bidrag til vektøkning + glykmisk dysregulering.Måtelig individuell RR men svært vanlig eksponering → stor absolutt befolkningstilttrekkende brøkdel. STUB i påvente av to-co-lead avtegn per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for tamoxifen: Prevention-persona RedFlag for tamoxifen exposure ≥5y in women with intact uterus. ~2-7 fold endometrial cancer risk. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending symptom-prompted evaluation (postmenopausal bleeding → immediate workup with TVUS + endometrial biopsy). Routine asymptomatic TVUS screening NOT recommended per ACOG (false-positives from tamoxifen-related subepithelial changes). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for transplan: Forebyggende person RedFlag for immunsuppression. Motorruter til forebyggingsplan med intensiv overvåking + redusere immunsosuppressiv diskusjon + målrettet screening.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for type-2 di: Prevention-persona RedFlag for type-2 diabetes mellitus as multi-organ modest cancer risk amplifier. New-onset T2DM ≥50 with weight loss has ~1% absolute 3-year risk of pancreatic cancer — actionable surveillance signal (EUS or MR-pancreas in high-risk subset per ACG 2022). Other cancer-risk contributions are background and modify population-screening adherence rather than triggering off-schedule imaging. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for very hot: Forebyggende tiltak RedFlag for svært varmt konsum av drikker ≥65 °C. IARC gruppe 2A klassifisering (2016). Viktigst i regioner med høy bakgrunns ESC insidens (Iran, Tyrkia, Kina, deler av Sør-Amerika), effekt liten i lavforekomst regioner. Motorveier til forebyggingPlanen anbefaler rådgivning om drikktemperatur. STUB i påvente av to-klinisk-co-lead avtegning pr. CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for vinyl chl: Forebyggende person RedFlag for vinylklorid → hepatisk angiosarkom / HCC. Pre-1974 PVC-arbeidstakere fortsatt i restrisiko. STUB i påvente av to-co-lead avtegning.
Prevention-persona RedFlag — v0.3 IARC 2: Prevention-persona RedFlag — v0.3 IARC 2A probable-carcinogen batch (2026-05-19). IARC Group 2A probable — limited human evidence; clinical recommendation more conservative than Group 1. IARC Monograph 112 (2015) is the canonical evidence anchor and is NOT yet a separate SRC entity in KB; cited in notes only. Evidence-base contestation: the IARC Group 2A classification is not concordant with EFSA / EPA / Health Canada / JMPR "unlikely to pose carcinogenic risk" conclusions. Primary IO resistance is operationally d: Primary IO resistance is operationally distinct from acquired resistance (PD after initial response >6 months). SITC consensus (Kluger 2020) defines primary resistance as PD within 6 months of IO start. Subsequent options vary by tumor: melanoma — BRAF/MEKi if V600E, T-VEC, TIL therapy at trial centers, IL-2; NSCLC — docetaxel ± ramucirumab, ADC if HER2/TROP2; urothelial — enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab combination remains active even after IO-mono PD per EV-302; RCC — cabozantinib monotherapy or lenvatinib + everolimus. IO-rechallenge is generally not standard but may be considered after >6 months treatment-free + non-PD discontinuation reason.

Primary Sjögren's syndrome (chronic autoimmune exocrinopathy with characteristic anti-Ro/SSA ± anti-La/SSB autoantibodies and histologic focal lymphocytic infiltration of minor salivary glands; EULAR/ACR 2016 classification criteria) in an individual without a current lymphoma diagnosis. The strongest hematologic-cancer risk factor among rheumatic diseases — ~15-20x relative risk for marginal zone (MALT) lymphoma, predominantly arising in parotid and lacrimal glands, with lifetime incidence ~5-10%. Risk concentrated in patients with persistent parotid swelling, palpable purpura, cryoglobulinemia, low C4 complement, monoclonal gammopathy, lymph- node enlargement, or high EULAR Sjögren's Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI). Provides supplemental elemental calcium: Provides supplemental elemental calcium (~40% by mass of calcium carbonate). Absorbed in proximal small bowel via active vitamin-D- dependent transcellular transport (saturable at low calcium intake) and passive paracellular diffusion (linear with concentration). Cancer-prevention rationale: intraluminal calcium binds free bile acids and free fatty acids in the colon, reducing their proliferative and pro-inflammatory effect on colonic mucosa; additionally calcium modulates epithelial cell proliferation/differentiation via the calcium-sensing receptor. Calcium Polyp Prevention Study (Baron NEJM 1999) and follow-on trials: 1200 mg/day elemental calcium reduced metachronous adenoma recurrence by ~15-20%.

Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly conve: Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly converted to FdUMP, FdUTP, and FUTP. FUTP misincorporation into RNA disrupts pre-mRNA processing; FdUTP misincorporation into DNA produces strand breaks. Backbone of FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, FOLFIRINOX, FLOT, and capecitabine-bridged regimens. Bolus and continuous-infusion (CIV) schedules differ in toxicity profile (more myelosuppression with bolus, more mucositis/HFS with CIV).
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporate: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporated into DNA and RNA, inhibits DNA methyltransferases → re-expression of silenced tumor-suppressor genes + cytotoxicity at higher doses. Backbone of MDS-HR, AML-unfit (with venetoclax), and CMML 1L therapy.
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycyt: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycytidine. Phosphorylated by deoxycytidine kinase (rate-limiting) to active metabolites gemcitabine diphosphate (dFdCDP) and triphosphate (dFdCTP). dFdCDP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, depleting deoxynucleotide pools required for DNA synthesis (self-potentiation effect — increases cellular dFdCTP). dFdCTP is incorporated into DNA, after which one additional natural nucleotide is added before DNA polymerase stalls — "masked chain termination" — making the lesion resistant to exonucleolytic repair. Cell cycle phase-specific (S phase) with G1/S blockade. PDAC backbone (gem-nab-pac MPACT, gem mono in frail), biliary tract cancers, NSCLC, bladder, NK/T-nasal lymphoma (SMILE), Hodgkin / DLBCL salvage (GDP).
Pyrrolopyrimidine antifolate that, after: Pyrropyrimidinantifolat som etter intracellulær polyglutamasjon ved folylpolyglutamatsyntetase samtidig hemmer flere folateavhengige enzymer som er kritiske for tymidin og purin biosyntese: tymidylatsyntase (TS — primærmål), dihydrofolatreduktase (DHFR) og glycinamidribocleotid formyltransferase (GARFT). Den kombinerte hemmingen forstyrrer både tymidylat- og purine de-novosyntesen, stanser DNA / RNA-produksjon og gir S-fasespesifikk cytotoksiøsitet. Aktiviteten er histologisk begrenset: svært aktiv i ikke-squamøs NSCLC og malign pleural mesoteliom (MPM), minimal til ingen aktivitet i flögulær NSTC på grunn av høyere referanseverdi for TS-uttrykk i fugebus histologi. R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AM: R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AML (~70-80% of IDH2-mut AML; ~6-8% of all AML). IDHENTIFY R/R AML phase-3 did not show OS benefit vs conventional care over all comers but enriched in IDH2-mut who had not received prior HMA. Combination with venetoclax + azacitidine under study. R175H is the most common TP53 missense h: R175H is the most common TP53 missense hotspot across all human cancers (~5-7% of TP53-mutant tumors per IARC TP53 Database). Structural class mutant — the R175 substitution to histidine disrupts the DNA-binding domain fold (zinc-coordination region). Beyond loss-of-function (LoF), R175H is a canonical example of mutant-p53 GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (GOF): the mutant protein acquires pro-oncogenic activities (chemoresistance via NF-kB, increased migration/invasion, metabolic reprogramming, chronic inflammation). Clinical implication: R175H+ tumors generally have worse chemo response than TP53-WT or even other TP53-mut tumors. In AML: TP53-mut (any) including R175H → very poor outcomes with intensive chemo, route to alloSCT or venetoclax-azacitidine + clinical trials. In MM: routes to quadruplet per high-risk cytogenetics composite. Emerging GOF-targeting strategies (eprenetapopt/APR-246, arsenic trioxide for structural mutants) are largely investigational; R175H specifically among the reactivatable structural mutants.
R248 is one of the six most-mutated codo: R248 is one of the six most-mutated codons in TP53 (along with R175, G245, R249, R273, R282). DNA-contact class: R248 sits in the L3 loop and makes direct base-specific contact with the DNA minor groove. Substitution to glutamine (R248Q) abolishes sequence-specific DNA binding while preserving overall fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H). R248Q has well-documented gain-of-function (GOF) activities in mouse models — accelerates tumorigenesis and metastasis beyond simple p53-null. Clinical implications mirror other TP53 hotspots: in AML/MDS routes away from intensive chemo toward venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT; in CLL/MCL/MM contraindicates chemoimmuno or routes to high-risk-cytogenetics regimens. Distinction from R248W (different substitution, also a hotspot) — R248Q tends to retain partial folding while R248W more disruptive; both are pathogenic.
R273 is among the top three most-mutated: R273 is among the top three most-mutated TP53 codons (with R175 and R248). DNA-contact class: R273 directly contacts the DNA major groove via its guanidinium side chain. R→H substitution preserves the thermal stability of the protein fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H) but eliminates specific DNA binding. R273H is one of the best-characterized GOF p53 mutants — promotes chemoresistance via NF-κB activation, drives invasion/metastasis through CXCR4 and RhoA pathways, reprograms metabolism (mevalonate pathway upregulation). Clinical implications mirror the TP53-mutant class: AML/MDS — venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; CLL/MCL — contraindicates chemoimmuno; MM — high-risk cytogenetics composite routes to quadruplet. Notably, R273H tumors are particularly resistant to platinum chemotherapy across solid-tumor types per multiple correlative analyses — relevant for ovarian, lung, esophageal cancer treatment selection.
R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codo: R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codon, often grouped with R248 and R273 as the canonical hotspot ring. Hybrid structural/contact mutant: R282 stabilizes the L1/S3 loop region adjacent to the DNA-binding surface, and R→W partially destabilizes the fold while altering contact geometry. Functional studies show R282W retains partial transactivation activity on a subset of canonical p53 targets (CDKN1A/p21, BBC3/PUMA at reduced levels) — termed "partial LoF" — while still gaining oncogenic activities. Clinically R282W behaves similarly to other hotspots: in AML/MDS poor chemo response → routes to venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; in CLL/MCL/MM high-risk regimen routing. Distinction from full LoF mutants (truncating, splice-site) may matter for emerging mutant-p53 reactivator drugs (eprenetapopt) where residual fold is required — R282W generally considered reactivatable in early-phase trials.

RB1 alterations (deletion, mutation) occur in ~30% of muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and are enriched in the basal/squamous-differentiated molecular subtype (~50%). RB1 loss is associated with resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors (which require pRb to exert G1 arrest). In urothelial cancer, CDK4/6 inhibitors are investigational (no approved indication); however, RB1 status is being evaluated as a predictive biomarker for CDK4/6 inhibitor non-response in HR+ cancers where bladder patients are enrolled in basket trials. Therapeutic implications in bladder cancer: (1) RB1 loss may associate with sensitivity to immunotherapy (higher genomic instability) — inconsistent evidence; (2) Basal/squamous subtype (often RB1-low) responds better to neoadjuvant chemotherapy than luminal subtypes; (3) No approved targeted therapy exploits RB1 deficiency in bladder cancer as of 2026. ESCAT IIIB: RB1 is a prognostic and potential therapeutic vulnerability marker in urothelial cancer; no approved targeted agent.

RB1 biallelic loss, together with TP53 loss, is the molecular hallmark of SCLC (~95% of cases have both). RB1 loss is not used to select therapy in SCLC (all SCLC patients receive the same backbone: EP/EC ± atezolizumab/durvalumab); rather, it is a diagnostic characteristic and potential therapeutic vulnerability. RB1 loss renders cells dependent on alternative cell cycle regulators (CDK4/6-independent E2F activation) — this is why CDK4/6 inhibitors have no activity in SCLC (pRb loss negates CDK4/6 inhibition). Investigational targeting of RB1-deficient SCLC: aurora kinase A inhibitors (alisertib — phase II, limited activity); EZH2 inhibitors (tazemetostat — RB1-null tumors may have heightened EZH2 dependence); LSD1 inhibitors; ATR/CHK1 inhibitors (replication stress in RB1-null context). ESCAT IIIB: RB1 loss is diagnostically informative and a conceptual therapeutic target, but no FDA-approved targeted therapy exploiting RB1 deficiency as of 2026.
RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (: RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (pRb), the master G1/S checkpoint regulator. pRb normally sequesters E2F transcription factors to prevent S-phase entry; loss of pRb → uncontrolled cell cycle progression. Clinical contexts: (1) Hereditary retinoblastoma: germline RB1 mutation → bilateral/multifocal retinoblastoma in childhood; lifetime elevated risk of osteosarcoma, SCLC, melanoma. (2) SCLC: biallelic RB1 loss + TP53 mutation defines the SCLC molecular signature (~95% of SCLC). pRb loss by IHC is used in pathologic diagnosis. No targeted therapy for RB1 deficiency per se; SCLC treatment is chemotherapy (EP/EC) ± atezolizumab. (3) Urothelial carcinoma: RB1 alterations in ~30% of muscle-invasive bladder cancer; associated with basal/squamous subtype; not currently targeted. (4) Breast cancer: RB1 mutations occur in ~10% of TNBC; RB1 loss predicts resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib) — pRb is the substrate for CDK4/6 that drives cell cycle entry; without pRb, CDK4/6 inhibition is ineffective. RB1 germline pathogenic variants cause heritable retinoblastoma (~40% of retinoblastoma cases) — bilateral / multifocal disease in 80% of carriers, median age at diagnosis ~12 months. Carriers face lifetime ~50% risk of secondary primary cancers (osteosarcoma, soft-tissue sarcoma, melanoma, lung, bladder); cumulative risk markedly elevated after external-beam radiation therapy (EBRT) — modern protocols avoid EBRT to mitigate. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per COG / Children's Oncology Group + International Retinoblastoma Consortium): pediatric ophthalmology with EUA (examination under anesthesia) starting in newborn period — every 2-4 weeks until age 1, then progressive lengthening to monthly → q3mo → q6mo through age 7, annual through adolescence. Cascade testing to all first-degree relatives mandatory. Lifelong secondary-cancer surveillance: annual skin exam, attentiveness to bone pain (osteosarcoma in adolescence/young adulthood), avoidance of unnecessary diagnostic ionizing radiation. ESCAT IIA.

Selpercatinib (LIBRETTO-001/-531; ORR ~70%, PFS ~25 mo in advanced RET-mutant MTC) is now standard 1L for advanced / metastatic RET-mutant MTC. Pralsetinib (ARROW) similar efficacy. Comprehensive germline + tumor RET / RAS testing at diagnosis is now standard (NCCN Cat 1 recommendation).

RET mutations are the defining oncogenic driver of hereditary and sporadic MTC: approximately 25% of sporadic MTC carry somatic RET mutations (M918T in ~50% of these), and hereditary MTC (Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A/2B, Familial MTC) is driven by germline RET mutations (C634R/W/Y/F in MEN2A; M918T in MEN2B; C611/C620/C630 in FMTC-risk MEN2A kindreds). Total prevalence of RET-mutant MTC: approximately 60-70% when germline + somatic are combined. RET-mutant status is the primary biomarker gate for selpercatinib over cabozantinib/vandetanib as 1L systemic therapy. LIBRETTO-531 (Wirth NEJM 2024, PMID 39133858) demonstrated selpercatinib superior to physician's choice (cabozantinib or vandetanib) in 1L advanced RET-mutant MTC: median PFS not reached vs 16.8 month...

Radiotherapy contraindicated or declined for early-stage NLPBL (nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma, WHO 5th ed). Major clinical scenarios: (1) Young patient with breast or thyroid field overlap — cumulative RT dose risk of secondary malignancy and cardiac toxicity unacceptable; (2) Prior RT to the involved or adjacent region — reirradiation risks exceed benefit; (3) Patient refuses RT after informed discussion. In all scenarios rituximab monotherapy (4–8 × R weekly) achieves ~94% ORR with ≥70% CR in early-stage NLPBL (Advani 2014, IELSG-37 data) and is the accepted standard alternative. RT remains the default for eligible patients where field is safe and patient consents (stage IA-IIA, ≤2 cm).

Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose d: Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose dexamethasone until progression) was the MAIA control arm (Facon NEJM 2019, PMID 30926586) and represents the standard-access first-line regimen for transplant-ineligible NDMM. MAIA control arm outcomes: ORR 75.8%, PFS HR (D-Rd vs Rd) 0.56 (95% CI 0.43–0.73), 30-month PFS ~53.3% for D-Rd vs ~37.8% for Rd. Rd continuous showed superiority over MPT and melphalan-prednisone in the FIRST trial (Benboubker NEJM 2014, PMID 25184863): PFS 26 months vs 21.9 months for MPT. Dose of dexamethasone: low-dose (40 mg weekly = "Ld schedule") is preferred over high-dose (480 mg/cycle); ECOG E4A03 showed equivalent efficacy and better tolerability with low-dose dex in NDMM (Rajkumar LANCET ONCOL 2010). Renal adjustment is critical: lenalidomide is ~80% renally cleared. CrCl 30-60 → 10 mg daily; CrCl <30 → 5 mg daily or 10 mg qod. Myeloma renal impairment often improves with therapy — recheck CrCl monthly and escalate dose when GFR recovers. Second primary malignancy (SPM) risk: CALGB 100104 and IFM 2005-02 documented elevated SPM (MDS/AML) with lenalidomide maintenance post-ASCT; risk applies to continuous Rd as well at smaller magnitude. Regular consumption of very hot beverage: Regular consumption of very hot beverages (≥65°C / 149°F) per IARC Monograph 116 (2016) — applies primarily to teas (especially traditional preparation styles in regions of Iran, Turkey, China, parts of South America with maté), but also coffee/water consumed at scalding temperatures. IARC Group 2A (probably carcinogenic) classification — associated with esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma (ESCC), particularly in regions with high background ESCC incidence. Mechanism: thermal injury to esophageal epithelium → chronic inflammation → field carcinogenesis. Note: at typical Western coffee/tea temperatures (<60°C), no association observed; coffee + tea per se are not carcinogenic. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 lifestyle pilot).

Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g: Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g/day per WCRF/IARC threshold. IARC Monograph 114 (2015) classified processed meat as Group 1 carcinogen for colorectal cancer (sufficient evidence). Each 50 g/day of processed meat increases CRC risk by ~18% (meta-analyzed RR ~1.18; WCRF/AICR convincing-evidence rating). Processed meat = sausages, ham, bacon, salami, cured/smoked/salted/preserved meat. Red meat (Group 2A per IARC, probable carcinogen) is a separate but overlapping concern — threshold ≥500 g/week for red meat. Mechanisms: N-nitroso compounds, heterocyclic amines, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, heme iron. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 lifestyle pilot).

Relapsed/refractory DLBCL with confirmed CD20 expression on malignant B-cells, post ≥2 prior systemic therapies including one anti-CD20 antibody-containing regimen (R-CHOP), CAR-T-ineligible or post-CAR-T failure — candidate for epcoritamab (CD20xCD3 bispecific T-cell engager; subcutaneous step-up administration). Pivotal data EPCORE NHL-1 phase 1/2 (Thieblemont 2023 J Clin Oncol): ORR 63%, CR 39%, mPFS 4.4 mo, mDOR 12 mo in 3L+ R/R DLBCL. Off-the-shelf alternative to CAR-T for non-eligible / bridging / post-failure setting. Distinct from glofitamab (different schedule: fixed 12 cycles vs continuous; IV vs SC). CD20-loss escape post-prior-anti-CD20 is a documented mechanism — re-biopsy advisable for late-relapse cohorts.

Relapsed/refractory DLBCL with confirmed CD20 expression on malignant B-cells, post ≥2 prior systemic therapies including one anti-CD20 antibody-containing regimen (R-CHOP), CAR-T-ineligible or post-CAR-T failure — candidate for glofitamab (CD20xCD3 2:1 bispecific T-cell engager; intravenous; fixed 12-cycle duration). Pivotal data NP30179 phase 1/2 (Dickinson 2022 NEJM): ORR 52%, CR 39%, mPFS 4.9 mo, mDOR 18.4 mo in 3L+ R/R DLBCL after fixed treatment course. Differentiator vs epcoritamab: fixed-duration (12 cycles ≈ 8.3 mo) vs continuous; IV vs SC; obinutuzumab pre-treatment 7 days before C1D1 reduces CRS. Off-the-shelf alternative to CAR-T. Often considered after epcoritamab failure in BiTE-sequencing strategies, though direct comparative data are lacking.

Reproductive history combining late first full-term pregnancy (age ≥30) OR nulliparity, AND short cumulative lifetime breastfeeding duration (<6 months total). Both factors independently confer modest increases in hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer risk (RR ~1.2-1.4 each) per Collaborative Group on Hormonal Factors in Breast Cancer + WCRF/AICR. Mechanism: cumulative ovulatory cycles + unopposed estrogen exposure + delayed terminal differentiation of breast ductal epithelium. Effect cumulative with other reproductive factors (early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, HRT). Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 reproductive pilot).

Reversible non-steroidal inhibitor of cy: Reversible non-steroidal inhibitor of cytochrome P450 aromatase (CYP19A1), reducing peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogens (estradiol, estrone). In postmenopausal women aromatase activity in adipose, breast, and other peripheral tissue is the dominant estrogen source — anastrozole 1 mg/day suppresses circulating estradiol by ~80-95%. Cancer-prevention rationale: estrogen exposure is the dominant driver of HR-positive breast carcinogenesis, and near-complete suppression of postmenopausal estrogen production reduces incidence of ER-positive breast cancer (and DCIS). IBIS-II RCT (Cuzick Lancet 2014, 12-year follow-up Lancet 2020): in 3,864 postmenopausal high-risk women, anastrozole 1 mg/day for 5 years reduced breast-cancer incidence by ~49% vs. placebo (HR 0.51) with durable benefit out to 12 years.

Also part of the IMspire150 triplet (atezolizumab + cobimetinib + vemurafenib) for previously untreated BRAF V600 advanced melanoma, where the addition of atezolizumab modestly extended PFS. Off-label in NF1 plexiform neurofibroma and RAS-mutant histiocytic neoplasms.

Revumenib (SNDX-5613), an oral menin inhibitor, is FDA-approved (Nov 2024) for relapsed/refractory KMT2A-rearranged acute leukemia (AML and ALL). AUGMENT-101 (Issa et al. NEJM 2023; Erba et al. ASH 2023 update): KMT2A-rearranged R/R AML/ALL — ORR 23% (CR + CRh + CRi), complete remission with full recovery 18%; mOS 8.0 mo. FDA accelerated approval based on remission rate as surrogate endpoint. KMT2A rearrangement is present in ~10% of adult AML (more common in secondary/therapy-related AML and infant leukemia). Menin is an essential co-factor of KMT2A-fusion oncoproteins — revumenib disrupts menin-MLL interaction, restoring differentiation block. Combination strategies under evaluation: revumenib + venetoclax + azacitidine (phase II ongoing). ELN 2022 risk: KMT2A-rearranged AML classified as intermediate risk (specific partner-dependent — MLLT3 intermediate; others may be adverse).
